## Appearance

Owen Ford is tall and broad-shouldered, featuring thick, brown hair. His face is distinguished by a finely-cut nose and chin, along with large, brilliant dark-gray eyes.

_Sources: [v4 CHAPTER 23 OWEN FORD COMES P8](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0008)_

## Personality

Owen Ford possesses a pleasant voice and a delightful smile. Around thirty to thirty-five years old, he aspires to write a great Canadian novel.

## History

A newspaper writer who previously published magazine short stories, Owen Ford suffered a severe case of typhoid fever and traveled to the sea to recuperate. While boarding in the area, he met Captain Jim, who shared his treasured life-book and stories with Owen, inspiring Owen to spend the summer writing a novel based on the old man's life. During his stay, Owen fell deeply in love with [Leslie Moore](../character/leslie-moore.md), though he initially felt forced to leave her without expressing his feelings due to her difficult circumstances. Upon returning to [Four Winds](../codex/places.md#four-winds) for a later visit, Owen declared his love to [Leslie](../character/leslie-moore.md) in the garden and was overjoyed when she confessed her love for him in return.

_Sources: [v4 CHAPTER 22 MISS CORNELIA ARRANGES MATTERS P19](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0019), [v4 CHAPTER 23 OWEN FORD COMES P23](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0023), [v4 CHAPTER 24 THE LIFE-BOOK OF CAPTAIN JIM P10](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0010), [v4 CHAPTER 24 THE LIFE-BOOK OF CAPTAIN JIM P21](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0021), [v4 CHAPTER 24 THE LIFE-BOOK OF CAPTAIN JIM P30](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0030), [v4 CHAPTER 24 THE LIFE-BOOK OF CAPTAIN JIM P37](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0037), +16 more_

## Quotes

> "Mrs. Blythe, this is a wonderful book—absolutely wonderful. If I could take it and use the material for a book I feel certain I could make the novel of the year out of it. Do you suppose Captain Jim would let me do it?"
>
> — Owen Ford — [v4 CHAPTER 25 THE WRITING OF THE BOOK P0](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0000)

> "You will give the soul and I the body. Oh, we’ll write a famous book between us, Captain Jim. And we’ll get right to work."
>
> — Owen Ford — [v4 CHAPTER 25 THE WRITING OF THE BOOK P6](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0006)

> "but in the main it’s done. I wrote the last sentence this morning. If I can find a publisher for it it will probably be out next summer or fall."
>
> — Owen Ford — [v4 CHAPTER 25 THE WRITING OF THE BOOK P19](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0019)

> "Yes—love triumphant and perfect. Leslie, you know—you understand. I have loved you from the first. And I KNOW you love me—I don’t need to ask you. But I want to hear you say it—my darling—my darling!"
>
> — Owen Ford — [v4 CHAPTER 38 RED ROSES P9](../source/v04-c38.md#nw-v04-c38-p0009)

> "But he must often be lonely. There was a touch of the seer about him tonight—he spoke as one to whom it had been given to speak. Well, I must be going, too."
>
> — Owen Ford — [v4 CHAPTER 38 RED ROSES P26](../source/v04-c38.md#nw-v04-c38-p0026)

## Relationships

### [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne-shirley--owen-ford.md)

[Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) and Owen Ford are close friends and correspondents who met when [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) guided him to his boarding house in [Four Winds](../codex/places.md#four-winds). [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) acts as a confidante for Owen, listening to his sorrow over his unspoken feelings for [Leslie Moore](../character/leslie-moore.md) and offering sympathy. Throughout his time in the area, they spend considerable time together discussing local history and collaborating with others on his novel draft.

### [Leslie Moore](../character/leslie-moore.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/leslie-moore--owen-ford.md)

Owen Ford and [Leslie Moore](../character/leslie-moore.md) share a deep mutual romantic affection. Upon first meeting [Leslie](../character/leslie-moore.md) at her household, Owen is immediately struck by her beauty, and they later form a close bond as she assists him with his novel draft over the summer. Though he initially grieves having to leave her behind due to her circumstances, Owen eventually returns to [Four Winds](../codex/places.md#four-winds), where he declares his love to [Leslie](../character/leslie-moore.md) in a garden and receives her eager confession in return.

_Sources: [v4 CHAPTER 23 OWEN FORD COMES P1](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0001), [v4 CHAPTER 23 OWEN FORD COMES P8](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0008), [v4 CHAPTER 23 OWEN FORD COMES P17](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0017), +14 more_

### [Uncle Jim](../character/uncle-jim.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/owen-ford--uncle-jim.md)

[Uncle Jim](../character/uncle-jim.md) (Captain Jim) and Owen Ford are literary collaborators who bond over Captain Jim's personal history. After discovering that Owen is the grandson of the schoolmaster's bride, Captain Jim shares his sea tales and lends Owen his life-book, which Owen turns into a novel during a summer at [Four Winds Harbor](../codex/places.md#four-winds-harbor). Captain Jim later gives Owen and [Leslie](../character/leslie-moore.md) his heartwarming benediction after the two declare their love for each other.

_Sources: [v4 CHAPTER 24 THE LIFE-BOOK OF CAPTAIN JIM P10](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0010), [v4 CHAPTER 24 THE LIFE-BOOK OF CAPTAIN JIM P21](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0021), [v4 CHAPTER 24 THE LIFE-BOOK OF CAPTAIN JIM P30](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0030), +10 more_
